Class PointGeospatial

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.attributetypes.SysMLAttributeType
sysmlinjava.attributetypes.PointGeospatial
All Implemented Interfaces:
ObservableAttribute
public class PointGeospatial extends SysMLAttributeType
SysMLinJava value type for the geospatial point in terms of a latitude and longitude in radians, and an altitude in meters.
All calculations are IAW the Aviation Formulary V1.47 by Ed Williams. Note that this formulary uses positive latitudes and longitudes for northern and western hemisphers, respectively, and negative latitudes and longitudes for southern and eastern hemisphers, respectively.
Author:
ModelerOne

    • distanceTo

      @Operation public DistanceMeters distanceTo(PointGeospatial otherPoint)
      Returns the distance, in meters, to the specified other point from this point. Uses the following formula to calculate distance in radiansm which is converted to meters, from the Aviation Formulary:
      
distanceRadians = 2 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin((thisLat - otherLat) / 2), 2.0) + cos(thisLat) * cos(otherLat) * pow(sin((thisLon - otherLon) / 2), 2.0)));
      Parameters:
      otherPoint - point to calculate the distance to.
      Returns:
      distance, in meters, from this point to other point.

    • headingTo

      @Operation public DirectionRadians headingTo(PointGeospatial toPoint)
      Returns heading in radians from this point to specified point. Uses following formula from Aviation Formulary:
      
 	d = <see calculation of d (distanceRadians) above>

	if (sin(otherLon - thisLon) < 0)
		heading = acos((sin(otherLat) - sin(thisLat) * cos(d)) / (sin(d) * cos(thisLat)));
	else
		heading = 2 * PI - acos((sin(otherLat) - sin(thisLat) * cos(d)) / (sin(d) * cos(thisLat)));
      Parameters:
      toPoint - point to which heading is to be calculated from this point
      Returns:
      heading in radians from this point to specified point

    • movedTo

      @Operation public PointGeospatial movedTo(DirectionRadians direction, DistanceMeters distance)
      Returns point to which this point is moved to along specified direction at specified distance. Uses following formula from Aviation Formulary:
      
	lat =asin(sin(lat1)*cos(d)+cos(lat1)*sin(d)*cos(tc))
 	dlon=atan2(sin(tc)*sin(d)*cos(lat1),cos(d)-sin(lat1)*sin(lat))
 	lon=mod( lon1-dlon +pi,2*pi )-pi
      Parameters:
      direction - direction (heading, bearing, ...) in radians along which to move this point.
      distance - distance in meters to move this point
      Returns:
      other point to which this point is moved to.

    • projected

      @Operation public static PointGeospatial projected(PointGeospatial firstPoint, PointGeospatial secondPoint)
      Returns a third (projected) point in a sequence projected from a first and second actual points for the case where the projected point is the same direction and distance from the first to the second point. This projection follows a "simple" algorithm.
      Parameters:
      firstPoint - first (actual) point in the sequence
      secondPoint - second (actual) point in the sequence
      Returns:
      third (projected) point in the sequence

    • normalized

      @Operation public PointGeospatial normalized()
      Returns a point that is "normalized", i.e. its longitude is within the range of 0 to 2*PI. Use this for positive-only longitudes, i.e. no negative longitudes for west of prime meridian.
      Returns:
      point with normalized longitude

    • isWithinRadialSection

      @Operation public boolean isWithinRadialSection(PointGeospatial apexLocation, PointGeospatial radialCenterLocation, DistanceMeters radialHalfDistance, DirectionRadians radialHalfAngle)
      Returns whether or not this point is within the specified radial section where the radial section is analogous to the segment on a dartboard.
      Parameters:
      apexLocation - point of the apex of the section (dartboard's target center)
      radialCenterLocation - center of the radial section, i.e. half way between left and right sides and near and far arcs
      radialHalfDistance - half distance between near and far arcs of section
      radialHalfAngle - half angle between left and right sides of section
      Returns:
      true if this point is within the specified radial section, false otherwise
